angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 493,251 km at 22.67 pc = 0.29 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 44.1087 +/- 0.0144 mas (same row, RUWE 1.02): 22.67 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.709 +/- 0.017 solar radii from Rescigno et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2134 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.550g1265R/abstract): 493,251 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.744 +/- 0.027 solar masses from Rescigno et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2134 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.550g1265R/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4580 +/- 50 K from Rescigno et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2134 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.550g1265R/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Rescigno et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2134 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.550g1265R/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2134.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.608, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
